idiopathic systemic
lupus erythematosus
(SLE).
adverse:
Drug-induced lupus-like
syndrome (arthritis, fever,
rash), reﬂex tachycardia,
angina precipitation, and
severe hypotension.
effects:
Headache, palpitations,
ﬂushing, anorexia, nausea,
and tachycardia.
notes:
Frequently triggers reﬂex tachycardia and ﬂuid retention; usually administered
alongside a beta-blocker and a diuretic to oﬀset these compensatory responses.

title: MINOXIDIL
action:
Potent direct-acting peripheral vasodilator that opens ATP-sensitive
potassium channels in vascular smooth muscle, causing hyperpolarization and
relaxation of arterial smooth muscle.
forms:
Oral tablets: 2.5 mg, 10 mg.
Topical solution/foam: 2%, 5%
(for hair growth).
indication:
Severe, drug-resistant
hypertension (oral),
and treatment of
androgenetic alopecia
(topical).
contraindication:
Pheochromocytoma
(can stimulate
catecholamine release),
acute myocardial
infarction, and
hypersensitivity.
adverse:
Marked reﬂex
tachycardia, severe ﬂuid
retention, congestive
heart failure exacerbation,
pericardial eﬀusion, and
cardiac tamponade.
effects:
Hypertrichosis
(excessive hair growth
on face/body), headache,
edema, tachycardia, and
weight gain.
notes:
Because it causes profound reﬂex tachycardia and ﬂuid retention,
oral minoxidil must always be co-administered with a loop diuretic
and a beta-blocker.

title: NITROPRUSSIDE
action:
Potent, fast-acting parenteral vasodilator that breaks down to release
nitric oxide (NO), activating intracellular guanylyl cyclase, increasing cyclic GMP,
and relaxing both arterial and venous smooth muscle
forms:
Lyophilized powder for
injection: 50 mg per
vial.
indication:
Management of
hypertensive
emergencies,
production of
controlled hypotension
during anesthesia to
reduce bleeding, and
acute congestive heart
failure
contraindication:
Compensatory
hypertension (such as
arteriovenous shunt or
coarctation of the aorta),
congenital optic atrophy,
and tobacco amblyopia.
adverse:
Severe cyanide/
thiocyanate toxicity,
profound acute
hypotension, and
methemoglobinemia.
effects:
Nausea, vomiting,
sweating, headache,
abdominal pain, and
apprehension.
notes:
Light-sensitive solution; infusion bags must be wrapped in opaque foil
during administration. Prolonged infusions risk cyanide accumulation.

title: DIAZOXIDE
action:
Opens ATP-sensitive potassium channels in vascular smooth muscle cells,
causing hyperpolarization and relaxation of arteriolar smooth muscle (direct
vasodilator). It also inhibits insulin release from the pancreatic beta cells.
forms:
Oral capsules: 50 mg.
Oral suspension: 50 mg/mL.
Intravenous injection: 15 mg/
mL.
indication:
Management of severe,
acute hypertensive
emergencies (IV form)
and treatment of
chronic hypoglycemia
caused by
hyperinsulinism (oral
form).
contraindication:
Functional
hypoglycemia,
hypersensitivity to
diazoxide or thiazides,
and conditions where
maintenance of blood
pressure or increased
cardiac output is
compromised.
adverse:
Severe hypotension,
sodium and ﬂuid
retention, ketoacidosis,
and hyperosmolar non-
ketotic coma.
effects:
Hyperglycemia,
tachycardia, ﬂushing,
dizziness, hirsutism
(excessive hair growth with
chronic oral use), and
gastrointestinal upset.
notes:
Because of its potent inhibitory eﬀect on insulin secretion, it is
uniquely utilized for intractable hypoglycemia, while its powerful
vasodilatory properties make it useful for acute hypertensive crises.

title: FENOLDOPAM
action:
Selective dopamine-1 () receptor agonist that causes vasodilation of
peripheral arteries (including renal, mesenteric, and coronary beds) and promotes
natriuresis and diuresis.
forms:
Intravenous injection /
infusion concentrate:
10 mg/mL.
indication:
Short-term management
of severe hypertension
(hypertensive
emergencies) when
rapid parenteral
reduction of blood
pressure is clinically
necessary, including use
during perioperative
care.
contraindication:
Hypersensitivity to
fenoldopam or its
components.
adverse:
Symptomatic hypotension,
tachycardia, intraocular
pressure elevation (in
glaucoma patients), and
hypokalemia.
effects:
Headache, ﬂushing,
dizziness, nausea, vomiting,
and anxiety.
notes:
Uniquely increases renal blood ﬂow and sodium excretion while
lowering blood pressure, making it particularly useful in patients
with renal impairment during hypertensive emergencies.

title: ALISKIREN
action:
Direct renin inhibitor that binds tightly to the active site of renin, blocking the
conversion of angiotensinogen to angiotensin I at the rate-limiting step of the renin-
angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS).
forms:
Oral tablets: 150
mg, 300 mg.
indication:
Treatment of
essential
hypertension, alone
or combined with
other
antihypertensive
agents.
contraindication:
Pregnancy (due to fetal
toxicity), and
concurrent use with
ACE inhibitors or ARBs
in patients with
diabetes mellitus or
moderate-to-severe
renal impairment.
adverse:
Angioedema, severe
hyperkalemia, severe
hypotension, and
acute renal
impairment.
effects:
Diarrhea (most common
at higher doses), cough,
dizziness, fatigue, and
nasopharyngitis.
notes:
Carries a black box warning regarding fetal toxicity; must be
discontinued immediately if pregnancy is detected.

title: CAPTOPRIL
action:
Inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE), preventing the
conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II, which decreases vasoconstriction
and reduces aldosterone secretion while increasing bradykinin levels.
forms:
Oral tablets: 12.5
mg, 25 mg, 50
mg, 100 mg.
indication:
Treatment of
hypertension,
congestive heart failure,
left ventricular
dysfunction post-
myocardial infarction,
and diabetic
nephropathy
contraindication:
History of ACE
inhibitor-induced
angioedema, hereditary
or idiopathic
angioedema, concurrent
use with aliskiren in
patients with diabetes,
and pregnancy.
adverse:
Life-threatening
angioedema (swelling of
face, lips, tongue), severe
hyperkalemia,
neutropenia,
agranulocytosis, and acute
renal failure.
effects:
Persistent dry hacking
cough, dizziness,
headache, fatigue, and
altered taste
(dysgeusia)
notes:
Contains a sulfhydryl group associated with speciﬁc adverse
reactions like rash and dysgeusia; should be taken 1 hour before
meal

title: ENALAPRIL
action:
Inhibits ACE, blocking the formation of angiotensin II,
lowering systemic vascular resistance, and reducing blood
pressure.
forms:
Oral tablets: 2.5 mg, 5
mg, 10 mg, 20 mg.
Intravenous injection (as
enalaprilat): 1.25 mg/
mL.
indication:
Treatment of
hypertension,
symptomatic
congestive heart
failure, and
asymptomatic left
ventricular
dysfunction.
contraindication:
History of
angioedema related
to previous ACE
inhibitor therapy,
pregnancy, and
hypersensitivity.
adverse:
Angioedema,
hyperkalemia, severe
hypotension (especially
with ﬁrst-dose diuresis),
and renal failure.
effects:
Persistent dry cough,
dizziness, headache,
fatigue, nausea, and
asthenia.
notes:
Long-acting ACE inhibitor that allows for convenient once- or
twice-daily dosing compared to captopril.

title: LOSARTAN
action:
Selective, competitive antagonist of angiotensin II type 1 ()
receptors, blocking the vasoconstrictor and aldosterone-secreting eﬀects of
angiotensin II.
forms:
Oral tablets: 25
mg, 50 mg, 100
mg.
indication:
Treatment of
hypertension,
reduction of stroke risk
in hypertensive
patients with left
ventricular
hypertrophy, and
treatment of diabetic
nephropathy
contraindication:
Pregnancy (fetal
toxicity) and
concurrent use
with aliskiren in
patients with
diabetes.
adverse:
Hyperkalemia,
severe
angioedema, acute
kidney injury, and
profound
hypotension.
effects:
Dizziness, fatigue, nasal
congestion, back pain,
and upper respiratory
infections.
notes:
Does not inhibit ACE or cause the persistent dry cough
characteristic of ACE inhibitors, making it an alternative for
patients who cannot tolerate ACE inhibitors.

title: CANDESARTAN, IRBESARTAN
action:
Potent, selective antagonists of the  angiotensin II receptor
subtype, preventing the physiological responses of angiotensin II without
aﬀecting bradykinin breakdown.
forms:
• Candesartan: Tablets:
4 mg, 8 mg, 16 mg, 32
mg.
• Irbesartan: Tablets: 75
mg, 150 mg, 300 mg.
indication:
Management of
essential
hypertension, heart
failure
(candesartan), and
nephropathy in type
2 diabetic patients
with hypertension
(irbesartan).
contraindication:
Pregnancy
(black box
warning for
fetal injury/
death) and
concurrent use
with aliskiren in
diabetes.
adverse:
Severe hyperkalemia,
acute renal failure,
symptomatic
hypotension, and
angioedema.
effects:
Dizziness, fatigue,
upper respiratory
tract infections,
diarrhea, and
dyspepsia.
notes:
Like all ARBs, they provide targeted RAAS blockade without
triggering the chronic dry cough seen with ACE inhibitors.

title: NITROGLYCERIN
action:
Converts to nitric oxide (NO) inside vascular smooth muscle, stimulating guanylyl
cyclase and increasing cyclic GMP. This leads to relaxation of vascular smooth muscle,
predominantly dilating large veins and decreasing preload.
forms:
•
Sublingual tablets: 0.3 mg,
0.4 mg, 0.6 mg.
•
Sublingual spray: 0.4 mg/
spray.
•
Transdermal patch: 0.1
mg/hr to 0.8 mg/hr.
•
Intravenous injection: 5
mg/mL.
indication:
Acute relief and
prophylaxis of angina
pectoris, management
of acute heart failure,
and control of
perioperative
hypertension.
contraindication:
Severe anemia,
increased intracranial
pressure,
hypersensitivity to
nitrates, and
concurrent use of
phosphodiesterase-5
(PDE-5) inhibitors
(e.g., sildenaﬁl).
adverse:
Severe hypotension,
paradoxical
bradycardia, reﬂex
tachycardia, and
methhemoglobinemia
(with high doses).
effects:
Throbbing
headache, ﬂushing,
dizziness,
lightheadedness,
and postural
hypotension.
notes:
Patients must maintain a daily "nitrate-free interval" (usually 10
to 12 hours) to prevent the development of pharmacological
tolerance.

title: ISMN, ISDN
action:
Organic nitrates that release nitric oxide, increasing cyclic GMP levels and
causing relaxation of vascular smooth muscle, reducing venous return (preload) and myocardial
oxygen demand.
forms:
• ISMN: Tablets: 10 mg, 20 mg;
Extended-release tablets: 30 mg,
60 mg, 120 mg.
• ISDN: Sublingual tablets: 2.5
mg, 5 mg; Oral tablets: 5 mg, 10
mg, 20 mg, 30 mg, 40 mg.
indication:
Long-term
prophylaxis and
management of
angina pectoris;
ISDN is also used
adjunctively in
chronic heart failure.
contraindication:
Concomitant use
with PDE-5
inhibitors
(sildenaﬁl,
tadalaﬁl,
vardenaﬁl), severe
hypotension, and
acute circulatory
failure.
adverse:
Severe hypotensive
episodes, syncopal
attacks, and
worsening anginal
attacks due to reﬂex
responses.
effects:
Severe throbbing
headaches, dizziness,
ﬂushing,
lightheadedness upon
standing, and nausea
notes:
Like nitroglycerin, these agents require a daily nitrate-free
interval to avoid drug tolerance loss of eﬃcacy.

title: VERAPAMIL
action:
Non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that inhibits calcium ion inﬂux
through slow channels into myocardial and vascular smooth muscle cells, reducing myocardial
oxygen demand, slowing AV nodal conduction, and dilating coronary arteries
forms:
Oral tablets: 40 mg, 80
mg, 120 mg.
Sustained-release tablets:
120 mg, 180 mg, 240 mg.
Intravenous injection: 2.5
mg/mL.
indication:
Treatment of
angina pectoris,
essential
hypertension, and
supraventricular
tachyarrhythmias.
contraindication:
Severe
hypotension,
cardiogenic shock,
second- or third-
degree AV block,
sick sinus
syndrome, and
ventricular
tachycardia.
adverse:
Severe heart block,
profound bradycardia,
acute heart failure
exacerbation, and
cardiovascular
collapse.
effects:
Constipation (very
common), dizziness,
nausea, headache,
and peripheral
edema.

title: DILITIAZEM
action:
Non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that inhibits calcium inﬂux
across cardiac and vascular smooth muscle membranes, producing coronary and peripheral
vasodilation and slowing heart rate/AV conduction.
forms:
Oral tablets: 30 mg, 60 mg, 90
mg, 120 mg. Extended-
release capsules: 120 mg,
180 mg, 240 mg, 300 mg,
360 mg. Intravenous
injection: 5 mg/mL.
indication:
Management of
Prinzmetal's variant
angina, chronic
stable angina,
essential
hypertension, and
rapid rate control in
atrial fibrillation/
flutter.
contraindication:
Sick sinus syndrome,
second- or third-degree
AV block (without a
pacemaker), severe
hypotension, acute
myocardial infarction,
and pulmonary
congestion.
adverse:
Complete AV heart
block, severe
bradycardia, acute
hypotension, and heart
failure exacerbation.
effects:
Peripheral edema,
headache,
dizziness, ﬂushing,
asthenia, and mild
constipation.
notes:
Balances vascular dilation with negative chronotropic and
inotropic eﬀects on the heart, making it eﬀective for both angina
and rate control.

title: NIFEDIPINE
action:
Dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that inhibits
transmembrane calcium inﬂux into vascular smooth muscle, leading to profound
relaxation of coronary and peripheral resistance arteries.
forms:
Extended-release tablets: 30
mg, 60 mg, 90 mg.
Immediate-release capsules:
10 mg, 20 mg.
indication:
Treatment of
vasospastic
(Prinzmetal's)
angina, chronic
stable angina, and
essential
hypertension.
contraindication:
Cardiogenic
shock,
hypersensitivity
to
dihydropyridines,
and acute
myocardial
infarction.
adverse:
Severe hypotension,
reﬂex tachycardia,
myocardial ischemia,
and peripheral edema
effects:
Flushing, headache,
dizziness, lower
extremity edema, and
fatigue.
notes:
Immediate-release forms should be avoided for treating acute
blood pressure spikes due to risks associated with rapid,
uncontrolled drops in pressure and reﬂex tachycardia.

title: AMLODIPINE
action:
Long-acting dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that inhibits
the transmembrane inﬂux of calcium ions into vascular smooth muscle and cardiac
muscle, causing peripheral arterial vasodilation.
forms:
Oral tablets:
2.5 mg, 5 mg,
10 mg.
indication:
Management
of
hypertension,
chronic stable
angina, and
vasospastic
(Prinzmetal's)
angina.
contraindication:
Known
hypersensitivity
to amlodipine or
other
dihydropyridine
s.
adverse:
Marked hypotension,
worsening angina
upon initiation in
patients with severe
obstructive coronary
artery disease.
effects:
Peripheral edema
(notably ankle
swelling), ﬂushing,
fatigue,
palpitations, and
dizziness.
notes:
Features a slow onset and long elimination half-life (around 30 to
50 hours), allowing smooth once-daily dosing without sharp peak-
to-trough blood pressure variations.

title: NICARDIPINE
action:
Dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that selectively inhibits
calcium ion inﬂux into vascular smooth muscle, resulting in preferential vasodilation of
cerebral and coronary blood vessels over cardiac tissue.
forms:
Oral capsules: 20 mg, 30 mg.
Extended-release capsules:
45 mg, 60 mg.
Intravenous injection/
infusion: 2.5 mg/mL.
indication:
Management of
chronic stable
angina and essential
hypertension; IV
form used for short-
term treatment of
hypertensive
emergencies
contraindication:
Advanced
aortic stenosis
(due to ﬁxed-
output
obstruction)
and
hypersensitivity
to nicardipine.
adverse:
Severe systemic
hypotension, reﬂex
tachycardia, increased
angina frequency, and
superﬁcial thrombophlebitis
at IV sites.
effects:
Peripheral edema,
headache,
ﬂushing, dizziness,
and nausea.
notes:
Provides signiﬁcant vascular selectivity, making it highly valuable
in neurosurgical or critical care settings for controlling blood
pressure

title: RANOLAZINE
action:
Antianginal agent that inhibits the late inward sodium current () in
cardiac cells, reducing intracellular sodium and subsequent calcium overload, thereby
improving myocardial relaxation and eﬃciency.
forms:
Extended-release
tablets: 500 mg,
1000 mg.
indication:
Treatment of chronic
stable angina
pectoris (often used
in combination with
beta-blockers,
nitrates, or calcium
channel blockers).
contraindication:
Pre-existing hepatic
impairment, and
concurrent use with
strong CYP3A4
inhibitors (e.g.,
ketoconazole) or
inducers (e.g.,
rifampin).
adverse:
QT interval
prolongation,
ventricular
arrhythmias, and
acute renal failure in
susceptible patients
effects:
Dizziness, headache,
nausea, constipation,
and asthenia.
notes:
Does not signiﬁcantly alter resting heart rate or blood pressure,
making it a unique metabolic antianginal agent for patients with
baseline low heart rates or blood pressure.

title: IVABRADINE
action:
Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channel blocker. It
selectively inhibits the  ("funny") ion current in the sinoatrial node, slowing the heart rate without
aﬀecting myocardial contractility or ventricular repolarization.
forms:
Oral tablets:
5 mg, 7.5
mg.
indication:
Reduction of hospital
admission risk for
chronic heart failure
in stable patients with
reduced ejection
fraction, and
symptomatic
treatment of chronic
stable angina.
contraindication:
Resting heart rate under
70 beats/min prior to
treatment, cardiogenic
shock, acute myocardial
infarction, severe
hypotension, third-degree
AV block, and severe
hepatic impairment.
adverse:
Severe bradycardia,
luminous phenomena
(phosphenes -
temporary visual
brightness changes),
and atrial ﬁbrillation.
effects:
Phosphenes (visual
ﬂashes),
bradycardia,
hypertension, and
headache.
notes:
Relies strictly on reducing heart rate to lower myocardial
oxygen demand; patients should be monitored for visual
brightness phenomena.

title: SILDENALFIL, TADALAFIL, VARDENAFIL
action:
Selective inhibition of phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE-5), preventing the
degradation of cyclic GMP (cGMP) in the corpus cavernosum. This sustains smooth muscle
relaxation and allows increased blood ﬂow to erectile tissue in the presence of sexual stimulation.
forms:
• Sildenaﬁl: Tablets: 25 mg, 50
mg, 100 mg.
• Tadalaﬁl: Tablets: 2.5 mg, 5
mg, 10 mg, 20 mg.
• Vardenaﬁl: Tablets: 2.5 mg, 5
mg, 10 mg, 20 mg.
indication:
Treatment of erectile
dysfunction, and
management of
pulmonary arterial
hypertension
(sildenaﬁl/tadalaﬁl)
and benign prostatic
hyperplasia
symptoms (tadalaﬁl).
contraindication:
Concurrent use with
any form of organic
nitrates or guanylate
cyclase stimulators
(due to the risk of
catastrophic, life-
threatening systemic
hypotension).
adverse:
Severe, profound
hypotension, sudden
vision loss (non-arteritic
anterior ischemic optic
neuropathy - NAION),
sudden hearing loss, and
prolonged priapism.
effects:
Headache, ﬂushing,
dyspepsia, nasal congestion,
visual disturbances (such as
blue-tinted vision with
sildenaﬁl), and back pain
(common with tadalaﬁl).
notes:
Tadalaﬁl is known as the "weekend pill" due to its remarkably long
elimination half-life of up to 36 hours, whereas sildenaﬁl and
vardenaﬁl have shorter durations of action (around 4 hours).

title: ADENOSINE
action:
Activates purinergic  receptors in the heart, inhibiting adenylate cyclase,
increasing outward potassium conductance, and blocking calcium currents. This results in a
transient, complete suppression of AV nodal conduction and automaticity.
forms:
Intravenous
injection: 3 mg/mL
(in 2 mL or 4 mL
indication:
Rapid conversion of
paroxysmal supraventricular
tachycardia (PSVT) to normal
sinus rhythm (including
tachycardia associated with
accessory bypass tracts like
Wolﬀ-Parkinson-White
syndrome), and diagnostic use
during myocardial nuclear
imaging.
contraindication:
Second- or third-degree
AV block, sick sinus
syndrome (unless a
functioning artiﬁcial
pacemaker is present),
bronchoconstrictive
lung disease (such as
asthma), and known
hypersensitivity to
adenosine.
adverse:
Transient asystole,
severe
bronchospasm, heart
block, and
ventricular
arrhythmias.
effects:
Flushing (very
common), chest pain,
shortness of breath,
dyspnea, nausea,
headache, and
lightheadedness.
notes:
Possesses an extremely short elimination half-life of less than 10
seconds; must be administered via a rapid intravenous bolus (typically
into a peripheral site close to the heart) followed immediately by a
saline ﬂush.

title: POTASSIUM ION
action:
Restores and maintains normal intracellular potassium concentration,
stabilizing the resting membrane potential of cardiac and skeletal muscle cells and
regulating neuromuscular excitability.
forms:
Oral tablets/capsules: 8 mEq, 10
mEq, 20 mEq.
Extended-rate oral powder
packets: 20 mEq, 25 mEq.
Intravenous infusion concentrate:
2 mEq/mL, 10 mEq/mL, 20 mEq/
mL.
indication:
Prevention and
treatment of
hypokalemia (potassium
deﬁciency) due to
diuretic use, digitalis
toxicity, or excessive
losses, and maintenance
of cardiac
electrophysiological
stability.
contraindication:
Severe renal
impairment
(oliguria/anuria),
hyperkalemia, acute
dehydration, heat
cramps, and
untreated Addison's
disease.
adverse:
Hyperkalemia leading
to fatal cardiac
arrhythmias,
ventricular ﬁbrillation,
and cardiac arrest.
effects:
Nausea, vomiting,
abdominal

title: MAGNESIUM ION
action:
Acts as an essential cofactor for numerous enzymatic reactions and blocks
neuromuscular transmission by decreasing acetylcholine release. It regulates sodium, potassium,
and calcium movement across cell membranes and controls cardiac excitability.
forms:
